overview: The Council voted to support state legislation restricting OxyContin prescriptions for minors and addressed public safety concerns regarding train gates and bus stops. Members also heard extensive public testimony regarding the Community Preservation Act ballot question.

items.title: West Medford Train Station Gate Safety
items.summary: Approved a resolution to notify the MBTA and Department of Transportation regarding safety incidents and traffic gridlock caused by frequently damaged gates at the West Medford station.

items.title: South Medford Bus Stop and Sidewalk Safety
items.summary: Referred a discussion on relocating bus stops and preventing illegal truck parking on sidewalks to the Transportation Subcommittee following concerns about pedestrian and wheelchair accessibility.

items.title: Craddock Bridge Rodent Control
items.summary: Approved a request for the Board of Health to investigate rodent issues caused by bridge reconstruction and for the City Solicitor to review potential financial remuneration for affected property owners.

items.title: Commendations and Election Meeting Cancellation
items.summary: Congratulated Teresa Castagnetti for being named Massachusetts Teacher of the Year and canceled the November 3, 2015 meeting due to the municipal election.

items.title: Support for State Bill Regulating OxyContin
items.summary: Approved a resolution supporting House Bill 3811, which prohibits prescribing OxyContin to minors under age 17, after a discussion regarding the opioid epidemic and medical necessity for chronic pain.

items.title: Public Discussion on the Community Preservation Act
items.summary: Heard public testimony from residents debating the merits and tax impacts of Ballot Question 1, the Community Preservation Act surtax.

items.title: Routine Business and Personnel Matters
items.summary: Referred a Garden Commission appointment to committee, approved a memorial sign replacement, and requested a legal opinion on excise tax waivers for deployed National Guardsmen.
